summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style overview of Bozeman, Montana, a city that is the seat of Gallatin County in southwest Montana. It covers the city's population figures from the 2010 census and 2016, its status as the principal city of the Bozeman Micropolitan Statistical Area, and its namesake founder John M. Bozeman. It also summarizes the city's incorporation and government history, its 2001 All-America City award, and notable local institutions including Montana State University, the Bozeman Daily Chronicle and Bozeman Yellowstone International Airport.
one_line: Overview of Bozeman, Montana: its population, namesake founder, government history, and key institutions.
key_facts: Bozeman is a city in and the seat of Gallatin County, Montana, United States.
The 2010 census put Bozeman's population at 37,280.
By 2016 the population of Bozeman rose to 45,250, making it the fourth largest city in Montana.
Bozeman is the principal city of the Bozeman, MT Micropolitan Statistical Area, which consists of all of Gallatin County with a population of 97,304.
The Bozeman Micropolitan Statistical Area is the largest Micropolitan Statistical Area in Montana and the third largest of all of Montana's statistical areas.
Bozeman is named after John M. Bozeman, who established the Bozeman Trail and was a founder of the town in August 1864.
The town of Bozeman became incorporated in April 1883 with a city council form of government.
In January 1922 Bozeman transitioned to its current city manager/city commission form of government.
Bozeman was elected an All-America City in 2001 by the National Civic League.
Bozeman is home to Montana State University.
The local newspaper of Bozeman is the Bozeman Daily Chronicle.
Bozeman is served by Bozeman Yellowstone International Airport.
